clue.text: Back in nick he died a very wealthy man

indicators.note: in tells us the turned letters go inside the word for nick

parts.note: to nick someone is to arrest or nab them

indicators.note: back tells us to read the letters for 'he died' from end to start

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, 'he died', seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A rich man ends up back in prison and dies there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' gives BO, which 'in' places inside the arrest word. 'Nick' looks like British slang for prison, but here it is the verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a European who made a fortune in India, hence any very rich man.

clue.text: Veteran is scared after refusal to jump

indicators.note: after places the scared word behind the other two

parts.note: no is a refusal
spring means jump
chicken means cowardly or scared

explanation.surface: An old soldier is frightened after declining to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no spring chicken is no longer young, an old hand.

clue.text: Bread sauce

definitions.meaning: bread is slang for money, and so is this word
sauce means cheek or impudence, as does this word

explanation.definitionFit: Brass is British slang both for money and for brazen cheek.

clue.text: German city left to Bolshevik leader after uprising

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the run of letters is read from the bottom up

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of Bolshevik

explanation.surface: A German town handed over to a Russian revolutionary chief after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns the whole run upward, since this is a down clue; 'after' is only a link. Bottrop is a real Ruhr city, so fair as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottrop is an industrial city in the Ruhr, in western Germany.

clue.text: There's nothing to equal passionate union meeting

parts.note: love means nothing or zero in tennis scoring
a match is an equal, as in 'no match for'

explanation.surface: A trade union meeting so heated nothing can rival it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union meeting' looks like a trade-union gathering, but 'union' belongs with 'passionate' as the definition and 'meeting' just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made for love rather than money or status is a romantic, ardent pairing.

clue.text: Learner taken to see Dutch artist painting in England

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is one

explanation.surface: A student goes to Ely to view a Dutch painter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like the verb, but means a cathedral diocese; Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter who worked at the English court.

clue.text: Deputy found fault, say, over split

parts.note: a vice is a moral fault

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the letters are flipped upward

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
a rent is a tear or split

explanation.surface: A stand-in is found to have a flaw, so to speak, over a division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EG into GE. 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicegerent exercises authority on behalf of a ruler, acting as their deputy.

clue.text: Pot with cut price plant

parts.note: a mug is a drinking pot

indicators.note: cut means the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: worth means value or price

explanation.surface: A pot bought at a reduced price to hold a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugwort is an aromatic wayside herb of the genus Artemisia.

clue.text: What lecture might be addressing

definitions.meaning: a lecture in the sense of a scolding or dressing-down
addressing someone means speaking to them

explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a reproof, and talking to someone is addressing them.

clue.text: Extremely thrilled, say, by Sappho (and a new translation!)

indicators.note: a new translation reworks the original words into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A reader is delighted by a fresh version of the Greek poet Sappho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new translation' rearranges SAY BY SAPPHO AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy as a sandboy is a British idiom meaning carefree and very contented.

clue.text: Know-all without a mark turned scarlet maybe

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go around the others
turned suggests the word scarlet is twisted into a new order

parts.note: M stands for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An unblemished know-all blushing red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges the colour as S...RTALEC, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps that around MA. 'maybe' just softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a conceited person who always thinks they know best, which is what a know-all is.

clue.text: Dance run in half-hearted fashion

indicators.note: half-hearted suggests losing part of the heart, one of the two middle letters of the word for run

parts.note: to gallop is to run fast

explanation.surface: Someone dances while jogging along without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in half-hearted fashion' drops one of the two central Ls from GALLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a lively 19th-century ballroom dance in quick two-four time.

clue.text: On the make? A possibility

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a make is a brand or type, which is a sort

explanation.surface: A one-line query about whether someone is a schemer out for gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the make' reads as the idiom for chasing profit, but it splits into a word for 'concerning' and a word for a brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is something one can turn to, an option, as in 'as a last resort'.

clue.text: Doing nothing in gym and in terrible disgrace?

indicators.note: terrible signals that the gathered letters are thrown into a mess

parts.note: O is the round figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Idling in the gym is shown up as shameful behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges O, IN, GYM and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is public shame or dishonour.

clue.text: Novice one cast originally in production of Peter Pan

indicators.note: in tells us the two letters go inside the rearranged title
a production of the play remakes its title words into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of cast

explanation.surface: A newcomer is cast in a staging of Peter Pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges PETER PAN to APPRENT...E, and 'in' puts I and C (from 'cast') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a beginner learning a trade, a novice.

clue.text: Celebrity's deed, perhaps, a contributor to writer's block

parts.note: note means fame or distinction, as in a person of note
a deed is one kind of legal paper, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A famous person's legal document is blamed for an author's creative block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' means a pad of writing paper, not the creative drought; each sheet contributes to the pad.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets of writing paper are what a writing pad is made of, so each is a contributor to it.

clue.text: The number of people who are unlucky in love

definitions.text: The number of people who are unlucky in love

parts.words: The number of people who are unlucky in love
parts.note: number means a song, so this is the kind of ballad sung by the lovelorn, not a headcount

explanation.definitionFit: A torch song is a sentimental song of unrequited love, from carrying a torch for someone.

clue.text: Nickname useless river

parts.note: a tag is a label or nickname
U/S is short for unserviceable, i.e. useless

explanation.surface: A dismissive label for a river that has no use.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian peninsula, reaching the sea at Lisbon.

clue.text: Farm' vehicle loaded with a weight of rocks

indicators.note: loaded with tells us the cart carries a letter inside it

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A farm cart carrying a heavy load of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded with' puts A inside CART. The 'rocks' are gems, so the weight is the unit for precious stones. The OCR's stray apostrophe after Farm is not on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is the unit of weight for gemstones, and rocks is slang for diamonds.

clue.text: Marks given to exercises during exam caused uproar

indicators.note: during tells us the pieces occur in the middle of the exam

parts.note: a test is an exam
M is short for marks, the old German currency
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Grades awarded for gym work in a test cause a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places the marks and exercises inside the exam word. 'given to' and 'caused' are link words; the definition is the noun uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm and, figuratively, a tumult or uproar.

clue.text: Unexpectedly meet resistance — woman in foul mood

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Una is a woman's name
cross means angry or in a bad mood

explanation.surface: Meeting resistance from a woman in a terrible temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' here is only a link word; the three parts are set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: Revolutionary left defending Italian stronghold

indicators.note: defending means the outer pieces surround and protect the inner one

parts.note: Jack Cade led a popular revolt in England in 1450
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A left-wing rebel guards an Italian fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' places the Italian abbreviation inside. Jack Cade led a 15th-century Kentish rebellion against Henry VI, so a classic crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, often one commanding a city.

clue.text: Cruel and stupid, getting in bad odour

indicators.note: getting in tells us the smell is placed inside the word for stupid

parts.note: inane means silly or stupid
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Someone is unkind and foolish and also smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' places the smell inside the word for stupid. Hum is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking compassion, so cruel.

clue.text: Part of flower that's not wild kept in tin

indicators.note: kept in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
tame is the opposite of wild

explanation.surface: A domesticated plant part preserved in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts TAME inside SN, the symbol for tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-bearing male organ of a flower.

clue.text: Fix up men for officer

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a jam is a fix or predicament
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone arranges men for an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns JAM into MAJ.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is an army officer ranking above a captain.

clue.text: Junkie's conduct after giving up heroin

indicators.note: giving up means letting go of something, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to usher is to conduct or escort someone
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: How an addict behaves after quitting heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' removes H from USHER. 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is drug-taking slang for an addict.

clue.text: Royalties offered to somebody in foreign currency

parts.note: K is king and R is rex or regina, two royal figures
one means a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Royal payments go to someone in a foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royalties' looks like payments to an author but means royal persons; 'offered to' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Latest book about party employee's crime?

indicators.note: about places the book next to the party word, round it in the reading order

parts.note: in means fashionable, the latest thing
a side is a party in a dispute or contest
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A newly published book about a party is linked to an office worker's misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is Job from the Bible. The question mark marks the definition as an example: an inside job is a crime done by someone within the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime committed by or with help from someone working inside the organisation.

clue.text: What's put on kippers might be, oddly, worth eating

indicators.note: might be signals the letters could form something else when rearranged
oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of worth

explanation.surface: Smoked fish whose dressing is odd but worth eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes WRH from 'worth', and 'might be' rearranges those with EATING. Kippers are smoked herrings, but here 'kippers' are sleepers, from kip, British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: People who kip are sleepers, and the clothes they put on for bed are pyjamas and nighties.

clue.text: Initially, mean to change vehicle

annotationWithheld.why: Initially, mean to change vehicle: the only parse found is SORRY (mean) with its first letter changed to L, but no clue word gives the L, so the wordplay is incomplete as printed.
